heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Elegoo Rapid PETG out of the box with exceptional consistency, reaching real-world print speeds up to 238 mm/s backed by a 20 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. While the stock stainless steel nozzle and enclosed chamber are fully capable, keeping the top glass vented during long prints prevents heat creep and nozzle buildup.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 20 mm³/s under Filament Settings to prevent under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm with 0.8 mm retraction to eliminate fine PETG whisker stringing.
Configure Part Cooling Fan threshold to keep the auxiliary side fan completely disabled (0%) to eliminate asymmetric part warping.
Set First Layer Flow Ratio to 0.98 to avoid PETG accumulation on the nozzle tip during initial squish.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and fine cobwebbing across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is highly hygroscopic and absorbs ambient moisture, lowering melt viscosity and causing post-retraction ooze.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6-8 hours in an active filament dryer, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm with 35 mm/s speed in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe bed adhesion causing PEI coating tear-out
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG molecularly bonds with smooth PEI surfaces under high bed temperatures.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVA glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue to serve as an interface release agent, and drop bed temperature to 75°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough top surfaces or nozzle dragging during high-speed infill
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Crossing infill lines with Grid pattern causes nozzle collision when printing rapid-flow PETG.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Change infill pattern to Gyroid or Cross Hatch in OrcaSlicer to prevent nozzle crossover on the same layer plane.

faq.question: Should the Bambu Lab P1S front door or top glass remain open when printing Elegoo Rapid PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, it is recommended to crack the front door or prop open the top lid by 1-2 cm during extended prints to maintain chamber temps below 40°C and prevent heat creep.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade the P1S stainless steel nozzle to hardened steel for Elegoo Rapid PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard Elegoo Rapid PETG is completely non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle provides full performance without wear.

faq.question: Why does the surface finish turn matte when printing at max speed (238 mm/s)?
faq.answer: Rapid cooling and extrusion at peak volumetric flow rate (20 mm³/s) limits polymer re-crystallization time; to restore a glossy sheen, lower outer wall speed to 100 mm/s.

faq.question: What Pressure Advance (PA) value should I set in OrcaSlicer for this combination?
faq.answer: The ideal calibrated Pressure Advance for Elegoo Rapid PETG on the P1S direct drive extruder typically falls between 0.032 and 0.038 s.
